text.arabic_uthmani: وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِۦ فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنفَقَ فِيهَا وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُشْرِكْ بِرَبِّىٓ أَحَدًۭا

words.gloss_range: opening connector that resumes the warning sequence into narrated aftermath
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens in continuation, so the ayah does not restart after the companion's warning. It carries the prior consequence logic into the passive destruction scene, making the ruined produce read as fulfilled aftermath before the owner's bodily and verbal responses appear.

topics.headline: aftermath after warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the destruction scene is continuation and fulfillment, not an isolated report.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows converge on the same local discourse payoff: the opening connector resumes the prior warning and launches its narrated aftermath.

words.gloss_range: completed passive encirclement of ruin with the affected produce marked through the following governed complement
words.root_gloss_range: enclosing, surrounding, guarding, besieging, and encompassing; locally the destructive encirclement branch is selected
words.prose: {{ar:أُحِيطَ}} ({{tr:uḥīṭa}}) is a completed passive event: the destroyer is not named, while the ruined produce is foregrounded through the following governed complement. The root's enclosure image gives the loss a no-exit shape, and same-surah encompassing-language at 18:91 can shadow the scene as a broader pattern of boundary and knowledge without making this verb a knowledge statement.

topics.headline: completed passive ruin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins with finished ruin and a withheld agent, so the owner reacts after prevention is already gone.
topics.reason: Local morphology and attachment support the completed passive event with the produce as the affected complement.

topics.headline: destructive enclosure image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the loss is pictured as an enclosure closing around the yield, while protective branches of the root are reversed rather than selected as the local sense.
topics.reason: The enclosure payoff survives, but root-family guarding and protecting senses must be treated as contrastive pressure under a destructive passive context.

topics.headline: same-surah encompassing thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this destructive encompassment can echo same-surah encompassing knowledge at 18:91, while the local verb remains physical ruin.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah echo is useful as contrast, but local grammar keeps {{ar:أُحِيطَ}} ({{tr:uḥīṭa}}) in the passive ruin frame rather than an active knowledge frame.

words.gloss_range: governed preposition marking the affected object of encirclement

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the later prepositional Lord phrase in the confession

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) supplies the governed path by which the passive encirclement lands on the owner's yield. As the first prepositional frame of the ayah, it also prepares the later {{ar:بِرَبِّي}} ({{tr:bi-rabbī}}) frame, moving from the object of ruin to the referent violated by association.

topics.headline: first governed ruin frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition is the grammar that fastens destruction to the produce and sets up the later theology-facing prepositional frame.
topics.reason: The rows share a local payoff: the first preposition marks the affected produce and participates in the ayah's two-frame movement.

words.gloss_range: possessed yield as the affected complement of the passive ruin; range includes fruit, produce, yield, and property by variant pressure
words.root_gloss_range: fruiting, yield, productive result, and accumulated property; locally a possessed productive output is destroyed

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby repeated particle or phrase in the ayah

words.prose: {{ar:ثَمَرِهِۦ}} ({{tr:thamarihi}}) is governed through {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}), yet semantically it carries the impact of the passive ruin. The possessive suffix makes the destroyed yield his own extension, and the word can carry fruit, produce, and property pressure through its root family and variant readings. Its return from the owner's earlier boast at 18:34 turns abundance into the named site of loss.

topics.headline: possessed yield as patient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the destroyed object is not anonymous produce but the owner's possessed yield, the first concrete extension of his identity to fall.
topics.reason: The grammar makes the noun genitive under the preposition, while the local semantic role still makes it the affected yield of the passive event.

topics.headline: fruit-yield-property range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the loss reaches beyond a single botanical item toward productive yield and property, while the standard local surface still names the possessed produce.
topics.reason: The broader economic range survives through root and variant pressure, but it should widen the local object rather than replace the standard surface noun.

topics.headline: boast reversed into loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same yield language from the owner's boast at 18:34 returns as destroyed yield in 18:42.
topics.reason: The same-surah echo has a concrete reference and a direct narrative payoff: the boasted productive sign becomes the locus of ruin.

words.gloss_range: resultative connector moving directly from completed ruin to the owner entering a response state
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the completed ruin into immediate consequence. The scene does not linger between destruction and response; the owner is carried straight into the state marked by {{ar:أَصْبَحَ}} ({{tr:aṣbaḥa}}) and the visible hand-turning that follows.

topics.headline: immediate consequence connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the narrative accelerates from finished loss to embodied response without an intervening explanation.
topics.reason: All rows point to the same local sequence-and-cause payoff for the result connector.

words.gloss_range: perfect inchoative verb introducing the owner into a new visible state, not simply reporting dawn-time
words.root_gloss_range: morning, becoming, entering a state, and morning exposure; locally the inchoative state-entry branch governs
words.prose: {{ar:أَصْبَحَ}} ({{tr:aṣbaḥa}}) makes the owner enter a new state after the ruin. Its predicate is the imperfect gesture {{ar:يُقَلِّبُ}} ({{tr:yuqallibu}}), so completed destruction becomes an ongoing scene of regret. The possible consequence voiced at 18:40 and 18:41 has crossed into accomplished aftermath. The morning-root field can add exposure and arrival-into-visibility, but local syntax selects state-entry rather than a simple timestamp.

topics.headline: state-entry frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owner is not merely doing an action; he has entered a sustained state whose content is hand-turning.
topics.reason: The local grammar strongly supports inchoative state entry, with the following imperfect clause as predicate content.

topics.headline: morning exposure pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a dawn/exposure coloring to the state change, while the verse does not require a literal dawn timestamp.
topics.reason: The root-family morning payoff survives as imagery of visibility, but local syntax keeps the selected function inchoative.

topics.headline: warning becomes fact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the possible consequence of 18:40-41 has crossed into accomplished aftermath in 18:42.
topics.reason: The boundary rows give a concrete narrative payoff: the prior warning frame is resolved as an accomplished state in the current ayah.

words.gloss_range: imperfect Form II turning, with repeated visible motion as the predicate of the state-entry verb
words.root_gloss_range: turning, overturning, reversal, and heart-related inner change; locally repeated hand-turning is selected
words.prose: {{ar:يُقَلِّبُ}} ({{tr:yuqallibu}}) is the ongoing predicate of {{ar:أَصْبَحَ}} ({{tr:aṣbaḥa}}), and its Form II shape makes the motion feel repeated: he keeps turning his two palms. The root's broader reversal and heart-field make the gesture more than mechanical, but the direct object keeps the local sense anchored in visible hand movement. Against 18:28 and the turning-back field at 3:144, this hand motion also joins a wider pattern of reversal without controlling the local parse.

topics.headline: ongoing repeated gesture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that regret is staged as an unfinished repeated action, not a single completed gesture.
topics.reason: The imperfect predicate under the state-entry verb and the Form II shape support the repeated visible gesture.

topics.headline: outer turning and inner reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that physical turning externalizes inner reversal, while the local object prevents reducing the verb to an abstract heart statement.
topics.reason: The root-family heart and reversal pressure survives as coloring of the visible gesture, but direct-object syntax keeps the local action concrete.

topics.headline: turning echo field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a same-surah and cross-surah field of turning and reversal, especially against 18:28, without letting those echoes govern the local parse.
topics.reason: Concrete echo rows survive as resonance, but local grammar remains the hand-turning predicate in 18:42.

words.gloss_range: dual possessed palms as the direct object of the repeated turning gesture
words.root_gloss_range: palm, open hand surface, edge, and restraint; locally two possessed palms are foregrounded
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَّيْهِ}} ({{tr:kaffayhi}}) makes the regret bodily exact: both of his palms are the object being turned. The dual and possessive morphology place his own exposed hand-surfaces in view, while the broader restraint field gives the image a failed-control edge without displacing the concrete palm sense. The geminated ff and ay diphthong add tactile sound-weight to the rare concrete palm form.

topics.headline: two possessed palms
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the gesture is not generic handwringing but the visible turning of both of his own palms.
topics.reason: Dual morphology, possessive suffix, and direct-object attachment all support the exact bodily tableau.

topics.headline: exposed palms and failed restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices exposed palm-surfaces carrying a failed-restraint undertone, while the local word remains a concrete body part.
topics.reason: The restraint-root pressure is meaningful as image and contrast, but local syntax selects the concrete dual palms.

topics.headline: rare tactile palm form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rare concrete palm form gives the scene tactile specificity and sound-weight.
topics.reason: The phonetic and rarity rows add a concrete payoff to the visible posture rather than a separate lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: preposition governing the open expenditure object as the ground or cause over which the palms turn
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) links the hand-turning to what he had spent, so the gesture is directed over the cause and object of regret. Its pressure differs from the later spatial {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), where the garden lies collapsed upon its supports.

topics.headline: causal grief over expenditure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first preposition turns the spending into the surface or cause of lament, while the later matching preposition marks physical collapse.
topics.reason: The local attachment makes the first preposition govern the expenditure object; the repeated preposition contrast gives it a distinct causal/postural payoff.

words.root_display: no lexical root (relative or maṣdar-like particle)
words.gloss_range: open relative object of spending, with process/object ambiguity kept available
words.prose: {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the relative clause that names the object of his regret: what he had spent in the garden. Because the form can be heard as relative object and as process-like, the phrase leaves expenditure open as both the invested thing and the act of investing.

topics.headline: open object/process of spending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the regret does not specify a neat itemized loss; it leaves the spent object and the spending process open together.
topics.reason: The relative-object parse is locally forced by syntax, while the maṣdar-like pressure survives as interpretive openness around the spending process.

words.gloss_range: completed Form IV spending/investing into the garden, now named as the object of regret
words.root_gloss_range: spending, causing resources to go out, passages/tunnels, depletion, and hypocrisy by root-family contrast; locally completed expenditure is selected
words.prose: {{ar:أَنفَقَ}} ({{tr:anfaqa}}) makes the investment a completed past act: the resources have already gone into the garden. Form IV supports the outward-flow sense of expenditure, and the root's passage/depletion field darkens the act as one-way loss. Wider links with false association and Lordship test the spending theologically, while hypocrisy and death branches remain background pressure rather than replacing the local sense of spent investment.

topics.headline: completed investment as regret object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that his grief turns on already completed investment, not merely on current property damage.
topics.reason: The perfect verb and local relative clause make the spent amount or act the object over which the owner turns his palms.

topics.headline: outward flow into loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the spending as resources sent outward into a place that can no longer return them, while the local sense remains expenditure.
topics.reason: Passage and depletion imagery survive as root pressure, but local Form IV and complement structure select spending/investing.

topics.headline: investment under theology
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ordinary spending language is reread under the later confession of lordship and association, while hypocrisy/death branches remain background pressure.
topics.reason: The theological collocations matter for the ayah arc, but they qualify the spending rather than making {{ar:أَنفَقَ}} ({{tr:anfaqa}}) itself mean hypocrisy or death here.

words.root_display: no lexical root (preposition plus feminine pronoun)
words.gloss_range: locative container phrase referring back to the garden as the destination of the spending
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) closes the spending clause by locating the expenditure inside the garden. The feminine pronoun keeps the garden as the container into which resources were placed, just before the circumstantial clause shows that same garden collapsed.

topics.headline: garden as investment container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the money did not merely vanish generally; it was put into this garden, the same referent now shown in ruins.
topics.reason: The rows converge on a local referent payoff: the pronoun sends the spending back into the garden and prepares the collapse tableau.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial connector introducing the garden as a simultaneous collapsed tableau
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) introduces the nominal ruin clause as a circumstance, not merely as another event in a list. While the owner turns his palms over what he spent, the garden is held in view as already collapsed over its supports.

topics.headline: simultaneous ruin tableau
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ruin is presented as the backdrop to his regret, a frozen state alongside the gesture.
topics.reason: The local nominal clause and circumstantial reading support the tableau payoff.

words.gloss_range: independent feminine pronoun making the garden the explicit subject of the ruin-state clause
words.prose: {{ar:هِيَ}} ({{tr:hiya}}) gives the garden its own subject position in the ruin tableau. The pronoun keeps the collapsed state grammatically pinned to the garden itself, not merely inferred from a suffix or from the owner's reaction.

topics.headline: garden as explicit ruin subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the garden itself is made the subject bearing the collapse state.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun and predication attachment support the explicit-subject payoff.

words.gloss_range: feminine active participle predicated of the garden, marking an ongoing empty/collapsed state
words.root_gloss_range: emptiness, hollowness, falling inward, and collapsed ruin; locally the garden is empty and collapsed as a state
words.prose: {{ar:خَاوِيَةٌ}} ({{tr:khāwiyatun}}) is the predicate of {{ar:هِيَ}} ({{tr:hiya}}), so the garden is held in a continuing ruined state. The active participle and feminine agreement make it one collapsed body, while the root's hollowing field makes the ruin feel emptied from within. The familiar collapse phrase has parallels at 2:259 and 22:45, but here it is anchored to this garden's supports.

topics.headline: durative collapse state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that collapse is not narrated as a passing event but displayed as the garden's ongoing state.
topics.reason: The active participle and nominal predication strongly support the durative ruin-state payoff.

topics.headline: hollowed empty ruin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ruin is both empty and collapsed, not merely visually damaged.
topics.reason: The root-family void and collapse senses are locally coherent with the support phrase and do not need correction.

topics.headline: formulaic ruin phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the garden is placed into a wider Quranic ruin formula also seen at 2:259 and 22:45.
topics.reason: The concrete references make the formulaic echo useful, while the local predicate remains this garden's collapse state.

words.gloss_range: spatial preposition governing the supports on which the garden has collapsed
words.prose: The second {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) is spatial: the collapsed garden lies upon its supports. Its repetition answers the earlier {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) over spending, shifting from grief over investment to architecture fallen on what should have held it up.

topics.headline: collapse upon supports
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prepositional turn from grief over expenditure to physical collapse upon supports.
topics.reason: The local complement relation and the repeated preposition contrast support a spatial-collapse payoff distinct from the earlier causal use.

words.gloss_range: plural possessed supports, trellises, roofs, or frameworks completing the collapse phrase
words.root_gloss_range: raised structures, trellises, roofs, frameworks, and throne language; locally garden supports are selected
words.prose: {{ar:عُرُوشِهَا}} ({{tr:ʿurūshihā}}) names the garden's own supports as the endpoint of collapse. The plural shows multiple framework pieces, while the feminine suffix binds them to the garden they failed to hold. Wider throne-language in the root family can sharpen the contrast between fragile worldly supports and lordship, but the local referent remains trellises or support structures.

topics.headline: failed owned supports
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the garden falls onto its own support system, making the architecture self-undermining.
topics.reason: The support noun completes the spatial phrase and makes the collapse land on what belonged to and upheld the garden.

topics.headline: framework ruin formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that trellises, roofs, and frameworks place the garden in a broader Quranic ruin-formula field at 2:259, 7:137, and 22:45.
topics.reason: The range and referenced parallels survive as ruin-formula pressure while remaining anchored to local garden supports.

topics.headline: fragile support versus sovereignty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a contrast between collapsed created supports and the wider root field of throne sovereignty, while the local word does not mean the divine Throne.
topics.reason: The throne branch is valid as contrastive root-family pressure, but local context selects garden support structures.

words.gloss_range: coordinator moving from visible gesture and ruin tableau into the owner's spoken lament
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the owner's speech with the visible regret scene. After palms and collapsed supports, the connector opens the lament beat where the bodily tableau becomes quoted theological confession.

topics.headline: gesture joined to speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lament is coordinated with the gesture, so speech grows out of the visible aftermath rather than replacing it.
topics.reason: The rows share the same structural payoff: the final connector moves the scene from embodied regret into direct speech.

words.gloss_range: imperfect speech verb introducing the quoted lament as ongoing narrated speech
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speech, declaration, and verbal performance; locally it frames a direct counterfactual confession
words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُ}} ({{tr:yaqūlu}}) keeps the owner's speech unfolding alongside the hand-turning. It governs the quote that follows, so the narrative pivots from visual ruin to a spoken confession. The speech root also reverses his earlier boast-speech at 18:34, 18:35, and 18:36 into regret, without making the verb anything other than the local quote frame. The lament also resonates with regret and mercy-speech contrasts at 18:49 and 18:98.

topics.headline: ongoing quoted lament
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah dramatizes the lament as present-feeling speech inside past narration.
topics.reason: The imperfect speech verb and quoted-complement attachment support the ongoing lament frame.

topics.headline: boast becomes confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owner's speech has changed from boast at 18:34-36 to confession in 18:42.
topics.reason: The same-surah speech recurrence supplies a concrete reversal in the owner's voice.

topics.headline: regret-speech resonance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lament participates in a wider regret-speech field, including 18:49 and 18:98, while the local function is still to introduce this quote.
topics.reason: The echo rows are useful as resonance but do not override the local quote-governing function.

words.gloss_range: vocative particle used exclamatorily to launch the regret formula
words.prose: {{ar:يَٰ}} ({{tr:yā}}) launches the direct-speech lament as an exclamation, not as a normal address to a present addressee. Joined to {{ar:لَيْتَنِي}} ({{tr:laytanī}}), it turns the confession into a cry of regret over an unavailable past.

topics.headline: exclamatory regret cry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quoted speech begins as a cry into absence, not as an informational statement.
topics.reason: The particle is locally licensed as the opening of the regret formula and carries exclamatory force.

words.root_display: no lexical root (optative particle plus first-person suffix)
words.gloss_range: counterfactual wish particle with first-person suffix, governing the wished non-association clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَيْتَنِي}} ({{tr:laytanī}}) turns the owner's speech into first-person counterfactual regret. The attached pronoun makes the wish his own, and the following negated clause supplies the impossible past he now wants to have been true.

topics.headline: first-person impossible wish
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the confession is not advice or doctrine in the abstract; it is the owner's own impossible wish about his past.
topics.reason: The optative particle and first-person suffix make the following negated clause a personal counterfactual regret.

words.gloss_range: past-negating jussive particle governing the non-association verb inside the impossible wish
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) puts the confession into negated past scope: he wishes he had not associated anyone with his Lord. The particle governs {{ar:أُشْرِكْ}} ({{tr:ushrik}}) and lets the final {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) complete the total exclusion under negation.

topics.headline: negated past inside wish
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the regret targets a past moral reality he cannot undo, and its negation remains open until the final universal object.
topics.reason: The jussive negator governs the verb and scopes over the final object, making the wished content a negated past confession.

words.gloss_range: first-person jussive Form IV verb of associating partners, negated under the counterfactual wish
words.root_gloss_range: sharing, association, partnership, and idolatrous association; locally negated partner-association with the Lord is selected
words.prose: {{ar:أُشْرِكْ}} ({{tr:ushrik}}) is governed by {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}), so the owner frames his regret as a wished negated past: that he had not associated anyone with his Lord. The verb names the theological fault only after fruit, spending, hands, and collapsed supports have been shown; its association field carries an entanglement or snare image while the local sense remains partner-association. It also echoes the companion's non-association wording at 18:38 and points toward the closing non-association command at 18:110.

topics.headline: jussive non-association confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the confession is grammatically precise: first-person, jussive, negated past, and completed by both the Lord complement and the final object.
topics.reason: Local grammar supports the jussive non-association frame and its two complements.

topics.headline: material loss names theology
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the material story resolves into the named theological fault of association.
topics.reason: The late placement of the shirk verb after the ruin scene makes the theological naming a central ayah payoff.

topics.headline: profession-regret-command axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same-surah axis: profession at 18:38, regret at 18:42, and command at 18:110.
topics.reason: The concrete same-surah references make the root echo a major structural payoff rather than a vague resonance.

words.gloss_range: required preposition marking the Lord as the referent with respect to whom association is denied

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the earlier prepositional produce phrase in the ruin frame

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is required by the association verb and marks the Lord as the referent with respect to whom partnership would be wrongly attributed. As the second prepositional frame, it answers the first {{ar:بِثَمَرِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bi-thamarihi}}): the ayah moves from produce hit by ruin to Lordship named in the confession.

topics.headline: Lord marked in association frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition fastens the Lord directly into the association frame and mirrors the earlier produce frame.
topics.reason: The local verb requires the prepositional complement, and the repeated preposition supplies the ayah-level frame from destroyed yield to violated Lordship.

words.gloss_range: first-person possessive Lord noun governed by the association preposition in the final confession
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, mastery, sustaining, nurturing, governing, and increase-related family pressure; locally personal Lordship is selected
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّي}} ({{tr:rabbī}}) makes the confession personal: the owner now says "my Lord" within the association frame. The possessive suffix interrupts third-person narration with owned acknowledgment, and the Lordship field names the sustaining authority his investment failed to honor. The word also echoes the companion's faithful wording at 18:38, but now in the ruined owner's mouth as regret.

topics.headline: personal Lordship confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the confession is personally owned: the violated relation is "my Lord," not an abstract title.
topics.reason: The first-person suffix, prepositional complement, and quoted speech context support the personal confession payoff.

topics.headline: sustainer versus investment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sustaining Lord is named after the garden investment fails, while increase and nurture branches remain theological pressure rather than alternate local senses.
topics.reason: The root-family sustainer payoff is central to the ayah arc, but increase-related branches should color rather than replace the local Lord noun.

topics.headline: companion word returns as regret
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the companion's confident "my Lord" at 18:38 returns as the owner's belated confession in 18:42.
topics.reason: The same-surah recurrence has a clear speaker reversal and must remain visible in later commentary.

words.gloss_range: final indefinite accusative object under negation, excluding anyone at all from association
words.root_gloss_range: one, anyone, someone, and uniqueness; locally indefinite anyone under negation is selected
words.prose: {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) completes the clause as the delayed object of {{ar:أُشْرِكْ}} ({{tr:ushrik}}). Because it is indefinite under {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}), the denial becomes exhaustive: not anyone at all. Its final position makes the ayah close on total exclusion, and its root can resonate with the oneness formula at 112:1 while remaining a common indefinite object here. Across the ayah, the opening encompassed yield is answered by this closing exclusion of every possible partner.

topics.headline: universal final object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the last word completes the negated verb with exhaustive scope: no possible partner is left outside the denial.
topics.reason: The local grammar strongly supports the indefinite object under negation as a universal exclusion.

topics.headline: oneness resonance without title shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices resonance with divine oneness at 112:1, while the local word remains an indefinite "anyone" object, not a divine title.
topics.reason: The oneness root echo survives as theological resonance, but local syntax blocks turning the common object into the divine name.

topics.headline: boundary arc closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens with encompassed produce and closes with excluded partners, framing ruin and repentance through total boundary-making.
topics.reason: The opening-to-closing rows give a concrete ayah-level arc from destroyed yield to universal partner exclusion.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive encompassing of his yield together with the garden lying fallen upon its trellises.
baseline_models.mechanism: Overwhelming enclosure takes the growing yield as wealth and ends by collapsing the productive canopy onto the supports that made it possible.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies overwhelming enclosure ending in ruin, making the passive event total rather than local.
The growing-wealth branch makes the object productive capital, not fruit alone.
The collapse branch supplies the downward failure of the garden's built order.
The vine-trellis branch identifies the supports on which the productive canopy depended.

changed_reading.before: A crop is destroyed and its owner laments the damage.
changed_reading.after: His whole yield-capital is overtaken, and the productive system collapses onto its own supports.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated turning of both palms over what he had spent in the garden.
baseline_models.mechanism: Face-to-face turning, literal palms, and expenditure as outgoing wealth make the gesture a recursive bodily audit: the hands that disbursed capital now display its absence.

activation_trace.role: Repeated face-to-face turning supplies the oscillating audit motion.
The literal palms embody what remains available to him after the outflow.
Expenditure as money leaving anchors the gesture in sunk investment.

changed_reading.before: He wrings his hands in regret.
changed_reading.after: His body performs a loss audit: the spending hands cycle over an investment that can no longer return to them.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: His spoken wish that he had associated no one with his Lord.
baseline_models.mechanism: The overlap between partnership, theological association, and lordship as ownership turns the confession into a correction of agency: no asset, ally, or claimant shares the Lord's governance.

activation_trace.role: The partnership branch exposes the shared-agency structure being revoked.
The theological-association branch fixes that revocation as a confession about God.
Lordship as ownership and mastery identifies the sole governing claimant.
The negative-context branch exhausts the class of possible partners without exception.

changed_reading.before: Material ruin prompts a generic renunciation of idolatry.
changed_reading.after: Ruin forces a proprietary correction: the wealth he treated as co-agent never shared the Lord's ownership or power.

context_deltas.mechanism: The garden begins inside a beneficial palm-ring, while an earlier punitive scene supplies destructive enclosure; at the focus, enclosure changes sides and takes the yield itself as its target.

activation_trace.role: The earlier occurrence supplies an active, overwhelming enclosure around wrongdoers.
The surrounding pavilion gives that punitive enclosure a bounded spatial form.
The ring around a center supplies the garden's original protective palm boundary.
The focus passive transfers overwhelming enclosure from an outer threat to the yield itself.

structural_cues: The window first presents destructive enclosure in 18:29, then a beneficial ring around the gardens in 18:32, then passive enclosure of the yield in 18:42.
The grammatical patient at the focus is the yield, so the former protected center becomes what is trapped.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: punitive enclosure and a palm-ring precede the focus passive. Reader arrow: the beneficial perimeter reverses into destructive capture. Alternative: the two enclosure scenes may remain parallel images without a deliberate reversal.

changed_reading.before: An external calamity happens to a well-protected garden.
changed_reading.after: The protection-image is inverted: the ring that marked secured abundance becomes a total enclosure from which the yield cannot escape.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier heedless heart follows its inclination; at the focus, no inner heart turns, but the owner's palms do. The missed inward reorientation is displaced into futile outward rotation.

activation_trace.role: The lapse from vigilance supplies the earlier interior failure.
The heart as understanding identifies the organ whose orientation had failed.
Inclination of the self supplies the directional pull followed by that heart.
The focus converts turning into a visible, repeated motion of the hands.
The two palms locate the belated reversal outside the heart.

structural_cues: The same QLB root names the heedless heart in 18:28 and the hand-turning action in 18:42.
The earlier sequence runs heart to desire; the later sequence runs hands to spent capital.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: a heedless heart follows desire, then palms repeatedly turn. Reader arrow: bodily rotation externalizes a reorientation the heart failed to make. Alternative: hand-turning may function only as a conventional regret gesture.

changed_reading.before: The palms merely display grief after the loss.
changed_reading.after: The body belatedly performs the change of direction that the desire-led heart did not perform in time.

context_deltas.mechanism: The owner's projected better return or outcome and his later repeated hand-turning share QLB: an anticipated profitable turn is answered by involuntary physical turning after loss.

activation_trace.role: The return-and-outcome branch supplies the better result he had projected for himself.
The face-to-face reversal branch makes the projected turn reappear as repeated bodily motion.

structural_cues: The nominal outcome in 18:36 and the intensive turning verb in 18:42 share QLB.
The boast about a better outcome precedes the collapse and the turning of empty hands.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the same root marks expected outcome and later hand-turning. Reader arrow: the second occurrence materially ironizes the first. Alternative: ordinary polysemy may explain the recurrence without an intended lexical answer.

changed_reading.before: His expectation of a better outcome and his later regret are separate moments.
changed_reading.after: His imagined favorable turn comes back inverted: projected return becomes the repetitive turning by which he realizes there is no return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The companion's earlier present-tense refusal to associate anyone with his Lord returns after collapse as the owner's counterfactual wish, making the confession delayed uptake rather than an isolated discovery.

activation_trace.role: The earlier theological refusal supplies the creed later echoed by the owner.
Repeated lordship fixes the earlier statement around the same governing relation.
Exhaustive negation completes the earlier formula that the focus wish repeats.
The focus changes the earlier live refusal into a wish about a missed choice.
The same exhaustive endpoint makes the verbal echo resolvable.

structural_cues: 18:38 and 18:42 share the sequence Lord, associate, anyone with only polarity and speaker-position changed.
The companion states the creed before the predicted calamity; the owner wishes for it only after the calamity.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: a near-identical formula is spoken earlier by the companion and later by the ruined owner. Reader arrow: the latter is belated uptake of the former. Alternative: both speakers may independently use a fixed monotheistic formula.

changed_reading.before: The owner independently discovers the right confession when ruin arrives.
changed_reading.after: He finally voices, in counterfactual regret, the exact stance already offered to him before the ruin.

context_deltas.mechanism: The boast of a stronger supporting group is answered by the absence of any faction able to help; the focus renunciation of any partner sits at the hinge where social capital is exposed as non-saving.

activation_trace.role: The supporting-group branch supplies the human backing in which the owner boasted.
Partnership language lets the confession revoke reliance on co-agents as well as possessions.
Exhaustive negation removes every candidate partner from the saving role.
A faction returning to its head gives concrete group form to the support that is absent.
Aid and making support manifest state the exact capacity his faction lacks.

structural_cues: The sequence moves from stronger group in 18:34, through the focus confession, to no helping faction in 18:43.
The indefinite 'anyone' in the focus is immediately tested by the total absence of human aid.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: a supporting-group boast precedes the confession and explicit non-support follows it. Reader arrow: the confession marks collapse of a social partnership model, not wealth alone. Alternative: 18:43 may simply narrate helplessness without expanding the sense of association in 18:42.

changed_reading.before: He regrets a private theological error while separately losing his supporters.
changed_reading.after: The confession also registers failed social capital: neither wealth nor the stronger group can act as a saving partner beside his Lord.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it cross-maps literal palms to the scale-pan branch and reads the sent hasban through accounting. It remains anchored in both palms, what he spent, and the packet's counting branch at 18:40. Render it only as an exploratory lexical overlay, not as the local lexical sense of either word.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Both palms turning over the expenditure after the predicted hasban reaches the garden.

activation_trace.role: The counting-and-account branch lets the sent calamity activate a counter-reckoning of the owner's investment.
The containing scale-pan branch lets the two empty palms resemble an improvised balance.
Actual expenditure keeps the balance image tied to the verse's economic object.

changed_reading.before: He looks at his hands while regretting sunk expenditure.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the empty palms become balance pans after a counter-reckoning: his private ledger is weighed by an event he did not control.

strongest_changes: The garden's protective enclosure reverses into an enclosure that captures its yield.
The hoped-for better return is answered by the repeated turning of the owner's palms.
The final confession becomes a belated echo of the companion's earlier creed and a recognition that social backing cannot save.
summary.what_was_special: The trace is driven by reversible spatial and lexical machinery: enclosure changes sides, QLB moves from heart to outcome to hands, and the same no-partner formula changes speaker and tense after collapse.
remaining_uncertainties: The QLB recurrence strongly supports irony, but ordinary polysemy remains a live explanation.
The link between punitive enclosure in 18:29 and the yield's enclosure in 18:42 is structurally strong but not made explicit.
The economic-partnership and empty-balance readings are activated by packet branches and should not be presented as exclusive lexical senses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Material enclosure reveals prior partnership.** `ش ر ك` B001 (“sharing and partnership”) is recognized only after the fruit is encompassed and the structure collapses. This retrospectively confirms 18:38: wealth had functioned as a partner in securing identity and future. I infer that loss reveals the hidden allocation of trust. His hand-turning and wish reverse bodily possession into belated diagnosis.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:52 and 18:102 showed hidden partnership recurring as failed cultic and protective relations.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Collapse exposes the vacancy inside apparent fullness.** `خ و ي/B001` is vacancy or empty space; `خ و ي/B002` is falling and collapse. The sequence removes surface stability (18:40), water access (18:41), then roof support here; 18:43 removes the social faction, and 18:47 exposes the whole earth after mountains move. I infer a scale-repeating mechanism in which supports are withdrawn until concealed emptiness becomes visible. `خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا` reads as structural diagnosis, not only a picture of ruins.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:43 removed social support, and 18:47 repeated the same exposure at earth-scale; the ruin became a miniature of universal stripping.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü bir kişi ya da topluluğun karşı koyamayacağı üstün bir gücün altında kalmasını, kişinin sonunun yaklaşmasını ve ürünün yok olup bozulmasını birlikte verir. lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnız edilgen kuşatılma yapılarında kişi, topluluk veya ürüne bağlanır; yalın bir çevreleme ya da genel yıkım anlamına genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi, topluluk ya da şeyin karşı koyamayacağı kuşatıcı bir gücün altında kalmasıdır; bu durum kişinin sonunun yaklaşmasına veya bir ürünün yok olup bozulmasına varabilir.

facets.statement: Etkilenen taraf, kendisini her yönden bastıran ve karşı koyamadığı üstün bir gücün altında kalır.
Bir kişi bakımından bu durum, sonunun ya da yıkımının yaklaşmış olduğunu bildirir.
Bir ürün bakımından kuşatıcı zarar, onun yok olup bozulması sonucunda gerçekleşir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal, gider ve harcama bildiren biçimlerle kişinin malını yitirip yoksullaşmasını bildiren özel yapıyı birlikte içerir; sonuç anlamı yalın biçimlere yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Malı veya başka bir şeyi zorunlu ya da gönüllü olarak bir amaç uğruna elden çıkarma ve bunun gider olarak elde kalmamasıdır. Kişi öznesiyle kurulan özel kullanımda elindekinin tükenmesi sonucu yoksullaşma anlatılır.

facets.statement: Mal veya başka bir şey, bir amaç uğruna verilerek ya da kullanılarak elden çıkarılır.
Elden çıkarma, kişinin kendisi ve geçindirmekle yükümlü olduğu kişiler için yapılan gideri kapsar.
Eylemin konusu yalnızca para değildir ve eylem zorunlu veya gönüllü olabilir.
Belirli kişi öznesiyle, elindekinin veya malının gitmesi sonucunda yoksullaşması anlatılır.
Bir kişi, çok gider yapan ve elindekini sıkça harcayan kimse olarak nitelenebilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyin iki ya da daha çok kişi arasında bulunmasını, tarafların birbirine karışmasını ve bir kişinin bir işe başkasıyla birlikte girmesini aynı ortaklık çekirdeğinde birleştirir. lexicalization_scope.note: Dal yalın anlamı temsil eder; tanım, belirli bir kalıba bağlı özel kullanımları bu genel ortaklık anlamına katmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin, hakkın ya da işin iki veya daha çok taraf arasında bulunması ve hiçbir tarafın onda tek başına olmamasıdır. Taraflardan biri diğerine katılabilir ya da onu aynı iş veya mülkiyet ilişkisine katabilir.

facets.statement: Bir şey, hak veya iş en az iki taraf arasında ortaktır ve taraflardan yalnız birine ait değildir.
Ortaklık, tarafların aynı mülkiyet veya anlam ilişkisi içinde birleşmesini ve birbirine katılmasını içerir.
Bir kimse bir başkasını işe, satışa veya mirasa kendisiyle birlikte dahil ederek ortak yapabilir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه رب الشيء إذا أصلحه وأتمه وقام عليه، ورب النعمة والصنيعة والضيعة والولد والصبي، والتربية حالا فحالا
يدخل فيه الرباني والربانيون بمعنى العلماء والحكماء وأهل العلم بالرب أو من يرب العلم ونفسه به
يدخل فيه الربة والجماعات الكثيرة، والربيون إذا فسروا بالألوف أو الجماعات، ورباب القبائل لاجتماعهم
يدخل فيه الربيب والربيبة للولد المربوب من زوج سابق، والراب والرابة لمن يقوم على أمره، والحاضنة
يدخل فيه الرُّبّ الطلاء الخاثر أو ثفل السمن والزيت، والسقاء والنحي والأديم والدواء والطعام إذا جعل فيه الرُّبّ أو أصلح به
يدخل فيه رب أو أرب بالمكان إذا أقام، ومرب الإبل ومرابها، وأربت السحابة أو الجنوب إذا دامت، والإرباب بمعنى الدنو
يدخل فيه الرباب والربابة للسحاب، والسحاب المتعلق أو المركب بعضه على بعض، وما سمي بذلك لتربية النبات أو دوام المطر
يدخل فيه الشاة الرُّبّى والرباب لقرب العهد بالولادة أو لزوم البيت للبن، وربان الشيء بمعنى حدثانه وطراءته، وربى الشباب
يدخل فيه الربابة للجلدة أو الوعاء الذي تجمع فيه القداح أو سهام الميسر، وجماعة السهام نفسها
يدخل فيه الربابة والرباب للعهد والميثاق والجوار، والأربة للمعاهدين، والرباب للعشور إذا جعل كالعهد
يدخل فيه الربة والربب لضرب من الشجر أو النبت أو البقلة التي تبقى خضراء
يدخل فيه الربب للماء الكثير، ويقال للعذب، من جهة اجتماع الماء
يدخل فيه الربرب لقطيع بقر الوحش، وقيل لجماعة البقر أو الإبل
يدخل فيه رب وربما وربت وربه كحرف خافض أو حرف معنى للتقليل، ودخول ما أو التاء أو الهاء عليه
يدخل فيه الربى بمعنى الحاجة، والرابة، والعقدة المحكمة، والنعمة والإحسان
يدخل فيه الرباني لرئيس الملاحين

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه ربا الشيء إذا زاد أو ارتفع، وربت الأرض إذا انتفخت وزادت، والرابي الزائد أو العالي، وأربى عليه إذا أشرف أو زاد عليه.
يدخل فيه الربوة والرابية والرباوة والرباة وما ارتفع من الأرض، مع اختلاف لغات الكلمة.
يدخل فيه الربا في البيع أو القرض، والزيادة على رأس المال، والربية لغة أو اسم خاص للربا.
يدخل فيه الربو بمعنى النفس العالي أو البهر أو الانبهار، وما يصيب الإنسان أو الدابة من علو النفس أو الانتفاخ من مشي أو عدو أو فزع.
يدخل فيه ربيت الولد أو تربيته بمعنى غذوته، وربا الولد أو الزرع بالنماء، وربوت أو ربيت في القوم بمعنى نشأت فيهم.
يدخل فيه الأربية أو الأربيتان بمعنى أصل الفخذ أو لحمتين ناتئتين في أصول الفخذين من باطن.
يدخل فيه قولهم جاء في أربية قومه أي في أهل بيته من بني الأعمام ونحوهم.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, sözcüğün olumsuzluk içinde konuşmaya konu olabilecek kişilerin bütün türünü kapsadığını ve yalnız tek kişiyi değil iki ya da daha çok kişiyi de dışladığını açıkça belirtir. Hazırlanan dal çerçevesi bu kapsamı doğru yansıtır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın birimin olumsuz cümledeki kapsamına bağlıdır ve başka bir söz öbeğine özgü anlamı bu dala taşımaz.

concept_map.definition: Olumsuz bir cümlede, söz konusu olabilecek kişilerden bir tekinin bile bulunmadığını ya da eyleme katılmadığını bildirir. Kapsam yalnız bir kişiyi değil, iki ve daha çok kişiyi de dışarıda bırakır.

facets.statement: Olumsuzluk altında konuşmaya konu olabilecek kişiler türünün tamamını kapsar.
Bir kişinin yanı sıra iki veya daha çok kişinin varlığını ya da katılımını da dışlar.
Bir yerde hiç kimsenin bulunmadığını veya bir eylemi hiç kimsenin yapmadığını söyleyen cümlelerde gerçekleşir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar olumsuzluk içindeki kullanımın kişi türünü bütünüyle kapsadığı konusunda birleşir. Böylece söz yalnız tek bir kişinin yokluğunu değil, o türe giren herhangi bir sayıda kişinin bulunmamasını da bildirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Olumsuzluk altında kişi türünün tamamını, sayı ayrımı yapmadan dışlayan doğal dal karşılığıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Olumsuzluk, kişi kapsamı ve birden çok kişiyi de dışlama birlikte korunur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir yerde kişi bulunmadığını bildiren varlık cümlelerinde doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişilerin tümünü olumsuzluk altında dışlama kapsamını korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir eyleme katılmama gibi yer bildirmeyen olumsuz bağlamları kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Belirli bir insan topluluğunun hiçbir üyesinin eyleme katılmadığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Belirli bir topluluğun bütün üyelerini olumsuzluk kapsamına alır.
error_profile.loses: Belirsiz bir yerde insan bulunmaması gibi topluluğu belirtilmeyen bağlamları kapsamaz.
